title: The release workflow had never run, and its first run could not publish
foundBy: session agent, on pushing the first v* tag this repository has had

evidence.verified: Run 34380809743 reports `completed success` after the trusted publisher was added, having failed on its first attempt with `npm error 404`. `@codesweep-ai/ui@0.3.0` is on the registry carrying an SLSA provenance attestation, which only a GitHub Actions run can mint, and the GitHub release `v0.3.0` exists. Nothing in this repository changed to fix it.

resolution: Fixed outside the repository, by adding release.yml as a trusted publisher for the package on npmjs.com. No commit resolves it, which is why evidence.commits is empty.
details:
`release.yml` had never executed. No `v*` tag had ever been pushed, so the entire publish path to the `latest` channel was unexercised code. `cs-lint oss` was reporting this as OSS-413, warning that the releases page INSTALL.md points at was empty, and it read as cosmetic.

Pushing `v0.3.0` ran it for the first time and it failed: `npm error 404 Not Found - PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/@codesweep-ai%2fui`. npm answers an unauthorised publish with 404 rather than 403, so this was a permissions failure.

The two publishing workflows are equivalent where it matters. Both declare `id-token: write` and both run `npm publish --provenance --access public`, differing only in `--tag dev`. `npm.yml` had published successfully minutes earlier. What differed was outside the repository: the package's trusted publisher on npmjs.com named one workflow, and `release.yml` was not it.

CONTRIBUTING says each package names its workflow as a trusted publisher, in the singular. Two workflows publish, so two need authorising, and the sentence hides that.

notes.text:
The shape is the one CUI-074 was about: a check that cannot run where you work reports its failure to whoever merges. Here it was worse, because the path could not run anywhere until a tag existed, and a tag is not something you push twice.

OSS-413 had been naming it for days. A warning that reads as cosmetic was in fact reporting that a whole publishing path was untested.
